title: The dependency is now the decision.
mainJudgement: The dependency is now the decision.

committeeQuestion.question: For one decision-critical journey, which external model, provider, market utility or component can change the outcome — and who can halt it?
committeeQuestion.why: Agent trading, AI-trading safeguards, payment-system supervision, dependency concentration and exploited vulnerabilities all put an external link inside the live decision path.
committeeQuestion.evidence: The end-to-end service chain, permitted action, control or market safeguard, intervention authority, current technical evidence, last test and the time needed to contain or pause the activity.

committeeQuestions.question: Where can automation influence a trading or customer outcome without a tested override and a reconstructable record of why it acted?
committeeQuestions.why: The practical market-integrity question is not whether the model was approved, but whether its live permissions, safeguards and intervention path can be demonstrated when the result matters.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The approved use, live configuration, input and output record, relevant safeguard, override test, exception log and accountable decision on continued operation.

committeeQuestions.question: When an exploit or supplier problem appears, can we identify every affected dependency and decide on containment within one business day?
committeeQuestions.why: A vulnerability alert or external disruption only becomes manageable when the actual dependency chain, practical alternatives and authority to act are known before the incident escalates.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The authoritative dependency record, affected services and components, exposure assessment, contingency or isolation action, time-stamped decision and any unresolved constraint.

judgement.title: The dependency is now the decision.
judgement.editorialAngle: External models, providers, market utilities and components now sit inside the live decision boundary.
judgement.distinctFromPrevious: Edition 14 asked whether the operating conditions for an activity still held. This edition shifts the focus to the dependency chain itself: the external link that can alter an outcome, weaken a safeguard or force a pause.
judgement.observation: Anthropic has examined agents transacting on users' behalf; ASIC has strengthened AI trading safeguards; ENISA has examined how dependencies weaken resilience; the Bank of England has set out its fees regime for recognised payment systems and specified service providers; and CISA has added newly exploited vulnerabilities.
judgement.executiveJudgement: The boundary is not the contract or platform label. It is whether management can identify the dependency, understand the permission or safeguard it affects, and act before a weak external link becomes a customer, conduct or market-integrity event.
judgement.implication: Pick one decision-critical journey this week. Trace it from the outcome to every external model, data feed, provider and exploitable component; put the one-page chain beside the escalation call tree and test who can halt it.

topSignals.label: Delegated action

topSignals.title: ASIC makes AI trading safeguards part of market-integrity discipline
topSignals.label: Live trading safeguard
topSignals.why: AI trading safeguards need to be designed into live deployment and oversight as part of demonstrating orderly and fair operation.

topSignals.label: External operating role
topSignals.why: The supervision of recognised payment systems and specified service providers makes the operational role of external services a direct management and regulatory concern.

topSignals.label: Service-chain resilience
topSignals.why: Dependency concentration can turn a disruption outside the firm into a live resilience event; the practical control is a usable view of the service chain and its alternatives.
topSignals.source: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity · Regulator · 2026-09-22
